newsitem.title: USA: Viacom's Redstone says Seagram reneged on deal.
newsitem.headline: Viacom's Redstone says Seagram reneged on deal.

text.p: Viacom Inc. Chairman Sumner Redstone Thursday accused Seagram Co. Ltd. Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. of trying to disrupt the companies' joint venture cable partnership by taking legal action against Viacom.

In his second day on the witness stand in Delaware Chancery Court, Redstone said Bronfman had assured him in March that Seagram would not sue Viacom over the launch of Viacom's new cable channel "Nick at Nite TV Land."
Canadian beverage firm Seagram filed suit in April, however, prompting Redstone to accuse Bronfman of trying to destroy the companies' USA Networks venture.
"Edgar your plan is to disrupt the partnership," Redstone said he told Bronfman. "You made an agreement, you reneged on an agreement."
"I don't want to be in a position of saying you're not telling the truth Edgar, but I haven't lost my marbles", Redstone tesified he told Bronfman.

Viacom, which owns Paramount Pictures, MTV and Nickelodeon, and Seagram, which owns entertainment and theme park concern MCA Inc., have been fighting for control of the cable partership, with each side accusing the other of violating the terms of their partnership agreement.
The case was put on hold last week to give both sides an opportunity to reach a settlement but the talks fell through.

At issue in the case is whether Viacom's launch of "Nick at Nite TV Land" and Viacom's operation of its MTV network violate the terms of the partnership which prohibits either company from operating or launching entertainment cable networks outside of the USA Network.
Viacom contends there was no breach of the partnership, that the partnership was working well and that MCA was trying to get control of USA Network "at an unfairly low price."

Redstone said he sought repeatedly to avoid litigation, even going so far as to waive a one-year non-compete clause to allow former Viacom executive Frank Biondi to take a top job at Seagram's MCA. In return, Redstone said Bronfman agreed to waive litigation against all of Viacom's MTV Network's cable operations.
Earlier this week Bronfman said he misspoke when he agreed to the blanket promise and testified the agreement was only intended to include a litigation waiver for TV Land.

Redstone's second day of testimony marked the halfway point of a scheduled four week trial. Even before the trial began Oct. 15, MCA lost a preliminary round when Vice Chancellor Myron Steele denied its request to exclude Thursday's testimony about the March agreement.

A source close to the trial said there has been no resumption of settlement talks since the two companies ended abruptly last week when Viacom withdrew its proposal to pay MCA $1.7 billion for its half of USA Network.
